"'''Rock with You'''" is a song by the American singer [[Michael Jackson]], written by [[Rod Temperton]] and produced by [[Quincy Jones]]. It was first offered to [[Karen Carpenter]], while she was working on her first solo album, but she turned it down.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://karenannecarpenter.blogspot.com/2013/04/behind-music-karen-carpenter-solo.html|title=Karen Carpenter Avenue: Behind The Music: Karen Carpenter (Solo)|website=Karenannecarpenter.blogspot.com|date=April 21, 2013|access-date=April 23, 2021}}</ref> It was released in October 1979 by [[Epic Records]] as the second [[Single (music)|single]] from Jackson's fifth solo  studio album ''[[Off the Wall]]'' (1979). It was also the third number-one hit of the 1980s,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Billboard/80s/1980/BB1980.pdf|title=Billboard|year=1980|website=Americanradiohistory.com|access-date=April 23, 2021}}</ref> a decade in which the pop singles chart would quickly be dominated by Jackson.

It reached number one on both the US [[Billboard Hot 100|pop]] (Jackson's third number-one on this chart) and [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|R&B]] charts (Jackson's second number one on that chart). It spent a total of four weeks at the top position on the former chart from January 19 to February 9, 1980, and five weeks (from January 5 to February 9, 1980) on the latter chart. According to [[Billboard (magazine)|''Billboard'']], the song was the fourth biggest single of 1980.<ref>[http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/yearend_chart_display.jsp?f=The+Billboard+Hot+100&g=Year-end+Singles&year=1980] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090520054312/http://www.billboard.com/bbcom/charts/yearend_chart_display.jsp?f=The+Billboard+Hot+100&g=Year-end+Singles&year=1980|date=May 20, 2009}}</ref> It is also considered one of the last hits of the [[disco]] era.<ref name="rollingstone_20140623">{{Cite magazine|url=http://www.rollingstone.com/music/pictures/50-best-michael-jackson-songs-20140623/10-rock-with-you-0273988|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140626033101/http://www.rollingstone.com/music/pictures/50-best-michael-jackson-songs-20140623/10-rock-with-you-0273988|archive-date = June 26, 2014|title = 50 Best Michael Jackson Songs|magazine = [[Rolling Stone]]|date = June 23, 2014}}</ref>

In Europe, the song was released as the third single from ''[[Off the Wall]]'', released on 1 February 1980.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=New releases: Singles|magazine=[[Music Week]]|page=24|date=2 February 1980}}</ref>

"Rock with You" was re-released as a single on February 27, 2006, as part of the ''[[Visionary: The Video Singles]]'' box set. In 2021, ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' placed it at number 354 on its list of [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time]]·<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-songs-of-all-time-1224767/michael-jackson-rock-with-you-1224984/|title = The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|magazine = [[Rolling Stone]]|date = September 15, 2021}}</ref>

"Rock with You" is a song by the American singer Michael Jackson, written by Rod Temperton and produced by Quincy Jones. It was first offered to Karen Carpenter, while she was working on her first solo album, but she turned it down. It was released in October 1979 by Epic Records as the second single from Jackson's fifth solo  studio album Off the Wall (1979). It was also the third number-one hit of the 1980s, a decade in which the pop singles chart would quickly be dominated by Jackson.

It reached number one on both the US pop (Jackson's third number-one on this chart) and R&B charts (Jackson's second number one on that chart). It spent a total of four weeks at the top position on the former chart from January 19 to February 9, 1980, and five weeks (from January 5 to February 9, 1980) on the latter chart. According to Billboard, the song was the fourth biggest single of 1980. It is also considered one of the last hits of the disco era.

In Europe, the song was released as the third single from Off the Wall, released on 1 February 1980.

"Rock with You" was re-released as a single on February 27, 2006, as part of the Visionary: The Video Singles box set. In 2021, Rolling Stone placed it at number 354 on its list of The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time·

It’s clearly a disco song — a four-four strut that fits right into the regular club BPM range}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/culture/music/michael-jackson-15-best-songs-ranked-mj-the-musical-thriller-bad-a3921906.html|title=From Thriller to Bad, Michael Jackson's 15 greatest songs on the London debut of MJ The Musical|first1=Harry|last1=Fletcher|first2=Jochan|last2=Embley|first3=Jessie|last3=Thompson|first4=David|last4=Ellis|first5=Zoe|last5=Paskett|date=March 27, 2024|newspaper=[[Evening Standard]]|access-date=September 6, 2025|quote=Rock With You is pure seduction, a lustrous piece of soulful disco that is as much a call to the dancefloor as it is to the bedroom. }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ultimateclassicrock.com/top-albums-1970s/|title=The Top 100 Albums of the 1970s|first=Michael|last=Gallucci|date=March 25, 2026|website=[[Ultimate Classic Rock]]|access-date=September 4, 2026|quote=...to the twinkling disco of "Rock With You."...}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Wyman|first=Bill|title=All 147 Michael Jackson Songs, Ranked From Worst to Best|url=https://www.vulture.com/2017/12/michael-jacksons-best-songs-ranked.html |work=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]|date=December 18, 2017|access-date=September 25, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.reuters.com/article/amp/idUSTRE56300320090706|title= How Michael Jackson's "Thriller" changed music business|publisher=[[Reuters]]|last= Gail Mitchell|first=Melinda Newman|date=July 6, 2009|access-date=July 30, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.treblezine.com/200-best-songs-of-the-70s/|title=Treble's Top 200 Songs of the '70s|first=Giovanni|last=Martinez|date=August 12, 2012|website=Treble|access-date=October 4, 2024|quote=Hitting the Billboard chart at No. 1 when it first debuted, Michael Jackson’s “Rock With You” is a genuine and impeccably crafted pop song.}}</ref>

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext:
The track received generally positive reviews from music critics. J. Edward Keyes of ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' said "What's remarkable about 'Rock with You' is how unobtrusive it is: a silky string section and barely-there twitch of guitar — Michael doesn't even hit the word 'Rock' all that hard — he just glides over it, preferring to charm with a wink and a smile rather than with aggression or ferocity."<ref>{{cite web|author=J. Edward Keyes|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-news/michael-jackson-the-essential-playlist-113986/ |title=Michael Jackson: The Essential Playlist|
publisher=[[Rolling Stone]] |date=June 26, 2009 |access-date=January 20, 2020}}</ref> Steven Hyden called it his "favorite song", and noted the line "Girrrrrrl, when you dance, there's a magic that must be love" as being "the most purely joyful moment [Hyden] has ever heard in a pop song".<ref>{{cite web|author=Steven Hyden|url=https://www.avclub.com/favorite-songs-1798215956 |title=Favorite songs|publisher=[[The A.V. Club]] |date=March 13, 2009 |access-date=January 23, 2020}}</ref> [[AllMusic]] highlighted the song on the album itself.<ref>{{cite web|author=Stephen Thomas Erlewine |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/off-the-wall-mw0000190332 |title=Off the Wall - Michael Jackson | Songs, Reviews, Credits, Awards |publisher=[[AllMusic]] |access-date=February 22, 2014}}</ref> [[Robert Christgau]] called it a "smooth [[Sentimental ballad|ballad]]".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ca.music.yahoo.com/read/review/12053010 |title=Michael Jackson |publisher=Webcitation.org |access-date=May 29, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100201050220/http://ca.music.yahoo.com/read/review/12053010 |archive-date=February 1, 2010  }}</ref> ''[[Cash Box]]'' praised the [[production (music)|production]], calling the song a "soft, classy number" with "multi-tracked harmonies," "a modified dance beat," "shimmering flute tones and jazzy guitar work."<ref name=cb>{{cite news|title=CashBox Singles Reviews|date=October 20, 1979|page=20|newspaper=[[Cash Box]]|accessdate=January 1, 2022|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1979/CB-1979-10-20.pdf}}</ref>
sections.text: The track received generally positive reviews from music critics. J. Edward Keyes of Rolling Stone said "What's remarkable about 'Rock with You' is how unobtrusive it is: a silky string section and barely-there twitch of guitar — Michael doesn't even hit the word 'Rock' all that hard — he just glides over it, preferring to charm with a wink and a smile rather than with aggression or ferocity." Steven Hyden called it his "favorite song", and noted the line "Girrrrrrl, when you dance, there's a magic that must be love" as being "the most purely joyful moment [Hyden] has ever heard in a pop song". AllMusic highlighted the song on the album itself. Robert Christgau called it a "smooth ballad". Cash Box praised the production, calling the song a "soft, classy number" with "multi-tracked harmonies," "a modified dance beat," "shimmering flute tones and jazzy guitar work."

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext:
A music video was released for the song, using the shorter single version. It features Michael in a sparkly sequined suit singing the song with a bright laser behind him. The video was directed by [[Bruce Gowers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/pictures/michael-jacksons-20-greatest-videos-the-stories-behind-the-vision-20140624/6-rock-with-you-1979-0598282|work=[[Rolling Stone]]|last=Weingarten|first=Christopher R.|date=June 24, 2009|title=Michael Jackson's 20 Greatest Videos: The Stories Behind the Vision|access-date=November 13, 2015}}</ref> and filmed in 1979 at the 800 Stage in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]].<ref>{{cite book|first1=Richard|last1=Lecocq|first2=François|last2=Allard|year=2018|title=Michael Jackson All the Songs: The Story Behind Every Track|chapter=Off the Wall|location=London, England|publisher=[[Cassell (publisher)|Cassell]]|isbn= 9781788400572|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CbVgDwAAQBAJ&pg=PT214}}</ref>

The music video was included on the video albums: ''[[Video Greatest Hits – HIStory]]'',<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.michaeljackson.com/us/music/michael-jackson-video-greatest-hits-history|title = MichaelJackson.com|access-date = November 13, 2015|website = Michael Jackson Video Greatest Hits HIStory {{!}} The Official Michael Jackson Site}}</ref> ''[[Number Ones (video)|Number Ones]]''<ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.allmusic.com/album/number-ones-dvd-mw0000999566|title = All Music|access-date = November 13, 2015|website = Number Ones [DVD] - Michael Jackson}}</ref> and ''[[Michael Jackson's Vision]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.michaeljackson.com/us/music/michael-jacksons-vision|title = MichaelJackson.com|access-date = November 13, 2015|website = Michael Jackson's Vision {{!}} The Official Michael Jackson Site}}</ref>
sections.text:
A music video was released for the song, using the shorter single version. It features Michael in a sparkly sequined suit singing the song with a bright laser behind him. The video was directed by Bruce Gowers and filmed in 1979 at the 800 Stage in Los Angeles, California.

The music video was included on the video albums: Video Greatest Hits – HIStory, Number Ones and Michael Jackson's Vision.

sections.heading: Live performances
sections.wikitext: Michael Jackson first performed the song on [[the Jacksons]]' [[Destiny World Tour]] on the second leg. He performed the song on [[the Jacksons]]' [[Triumph Tour]] and [[Victory Tour (The Jacksons tour)|Victory Tour]]. He performed the song on his solo world tour [[Bad (tour)|Bad]]. He also performed the song during the [[HIStory World Tour]], as a part of the ''[[Off the Wall (album)|Off the Wall]]'' medley (also featuring "Off the Wall" and "Don't Stop Til' You Get Enough") in certain concerts. "Rock with You" was rehearsed for the [[Dangerous World Tour]], but was not performed. Jackson also would have performed it for the [[This Is It (concert residency)|This Is It]] concert series, but the shows were canceled, due to his sudden death.
sections.text: Michael Jackson first performed the song on the Jacksons' Destiny World Tour on the second leg. He performed the song on the Jacksons' Triumph Tour and Victory Tour. He performed the song on his solo world tour Bad. He also performed the song during the HIStory World Tour, as a part of the Off the Wall medley (also featuring "Off the Wall" and "Don't Stop Til' You Get Enough") in certain concerts. "Rock with You" was rehearsed for the Dangerous World Tour, but was not performed. Jackson also would have performed it for the This Is It concert series, but the shows were canceled, due to his sudden death.

sections.heading: Mixes
sections.wikitext:
* Original LP version – 3:39
** This "classic" version was only released on initial runs of the LP record and cassette, as well as certain CD pressings manufactured in Japan, up to and including a Japanese-market version released in 1991. It was replaced by the full version of the 7" remix on later LP pressings and all other CD editions. The original version was later remastered and released on the "French Fans' Selection" deluxe box set edition of ''[[King of Pop (album)|King of Pop]]''.
* 7" remix video edit – 3:23
** The "remix" was used for the single and to underscore the video. The remix re-pans the guitar, and adds more strings, horns, and hand claps in the chorus. An edit was made to the middle musical bridge by adding fingersnaps and shortening it from two parts to just one.
* 7" version – 3:39
** This is the same as the 7" remix, but with the musical bridge left intact. This version appears on later pressings of the album.
* Extended version – 4:57
** Available only on the Japanese 12" promo, "Rock with You / Robin Hood". The latter song was recorded by Fox and the Promes.
* Masters at Work remix – 5:29
* Frankie's Favorite club mix – 7:49
* Frankie Knuckles radio mix – 3:50
** The Masters at Work remix and Frankie Knuckles remixes all contain previously unheard vocals and ad-libs not heard on the original album version. This is because the remixers were given access to the master tapes of the song to produce their remix. The master tapes contained additional vocals and cuts that didn't make it onto the original album version.
* Live 1981 (3:55)
** The live version, taken from the 1981 album ''[[The Jacksons Live!]]'', was included on the UK 12" "Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'" single in 1983.
* Live 1988 (4:05)
** The live version, included in the deluxe edition of ''[[Bad 25]]'' and on the DVD ''[[Live at Wembley July 16, 1988]]'', was recorded during one of the shows at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] during the [[Bad (tour)|Bad]] tour.
